newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures up, but NY arbitrage balloons.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures up, but NY arbitrage balloons.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures failed to regain an upward momentum on Tuesday afternoon despite soaring New York-listed arabicas and prices ended the day with pared gains.
"Again London failed to impress," said one. July/July arbitrage against London widened to new record high of 156.43 cents a lb as New York scaled new life-of-contract high of 240.50 cents.

Benchmark July broke the key $1,820 resistance early in the session to race up to $1,835, the highest since May 1996. But it fell back to $1,815 by lunchtime and stayed at that level by the close for a $40 gain.
A breakthrough above $1,820, the March 11 peak, triggered additional fund buying but scale-up hedge selling took some steam off the market, traders said.
Technically, London would now have to clear today's high of $1,835, seen as the immediate resistance, before testing the next level at $1,860.

The market has been gearing up for the move to above $1,800 since mid-March. Traders said a foothold above $1,800 was likely to be sustained since the majority of the origins had completed their hedge selling.
On the downside, a chart gap between $1,793 and $1,800 would serve as an immediate support.
Roasters, who were much better covered against July, moved out further forward to September, which firmed $36 at $1,831 but off its intraday high of $1,850.
The day's volume of 6,480 lots, which was dominated by July and September, was boosted by deals by jobbers.
Options volume of 1,314 lots was fairly modest, with interest centred on the forward September $2,000, $2,100 and $2,220 calls.
New York arabica rallied again on Tuesday as commission house buying triggered a succession of buy orders.
Some traders in New York said long-term weather outlooks calling for a cool air mass to make its way into Brazil inspired Tuesday's buying spree. But weathermen warned the chance of frost was slim.

The earliest crop-damaging freeze on record was May 30-31. June and July are the two dangerous months and in 1994, two frosts devastated Brazil's crop and sent futures prices to the highest in a decade. --Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
